predecessors.name: Habsburg monarchy
predecessors.text: Upper Hungary ('most of present-day Slovakia' and part of north-eastern Hungary), Royal Hungary under the Habsburg king until the rising led by Imre Thököly

predecessors.name: Principality of Transylvania
predecessors.text: the north-western counties (Nikolsburg grant of 1621) that Cliopatria draws in Upper Hungary from 1683: 23,014 km2

successors.name: Habsburg monarchy
successors.text: Upper Hungary, which the infobox hands back to the 'Kingdom of Hungary' (the Habsburg king's): Slovakia and the rest not drawn in Transylvania

successors.name: Principality of Transylvania
successors.text: the north-western counties drawn in Transylvania again in Cliopatria's 1687 shape

rulers.name: Imre (Emeric) Thököly
rulers.title: Prince of Upper Hungary ('King of Upper Hungary' in the Thököly article)

ledger.x: 1682: Thököly founds the Principality of Upper Hungary at Kassa as an Ottoman vassal.
19 November 1682: 23,014 km2 that Cliopatria holds in Transylvania up to 1682 lie in Upper Hungary from 1683.
1685: the Habsburg campaign reaches Upper Hungary.
15 October 1685: the contest ends with the realm.
15 October 1685: Upper Hungary reverts to the Habsburg king of Hungary.
15 October 1685: the north-western counties go back to the Transylvania row of Cliopatria (1687 shape).
15 October 1685: Thököly's principality ceases to exist.

wars.name: Thököly's uprising
wars.outcome: Thököly's war 'began in 1678'; Eastern Hungarian Kingdom lands and 'central Hungarian mining towns were soon in Thököly's possession'; the Ottomans recognized him in 1682 as Prince (King) of Upper Hungary; the 1685 campaign 'was a series of disasters', he was…

wars.name: Battle of Vienna
wars.outcome: 'Thököly materially assisted the Turks in the Battle of Vienna in 1683'; the Ottoman defeat began the Habsburg reconquest of Hungary.

certainty.note: A short-lived rebel-and-vassal state with no treaty or survey line; the western frontier ran to the Váh river approximately.
